questions.q: Why did saying farewell to the monkeys take such a long time?
choices: Thousands of monkeys all wanted to shake the Doctor's hand
The monkeys kept begging the Doctor to stay
The Doctor had to give every monkey a last dose of medicine
The monkeys had a long song to sing for each of the animals
questions.evidence: all those thousands of monkeys wanted to shake John Dolittle by the hand

questions.q: Why did Polynesia say they must tread softly and talk low?
choices: They might wake up the lions sleeping in their dens
The King might hear them and send soldiers to catch them again
The pushmi-pullyu was very shy and did not like loud noises at all
There were dangerous snakes hiding in the jungle-paths
questions.evidence: If the King should hear us, he will send his soldiers to catch us again

questions.q: What happened while Chee-Chee was away looking for cocoanuts?
choices: The King's soldiers found Chee-Chee and locked him up in the dungeon
The Doctor and the other animals got lost in the deep woods
Polynesia flew ahead to the beach to look for a boat to sail home
The pushmi-pullyu got frightened and ran back into the jungle alone
questions.evidence: got lost in the deep woods

questions.q: Where did the lost travelers end up after many days of wandering?
choices: On the seashore near the rocks where their ship had sunk
In the King's back-garden, by mistake
At the edge of the river where the monkeys had made their bridge
Back in the Land of the Monkeys, by the great stone
questions.evidence: they walked right into the King's back-garden by mistake

questions.q: What work did the King say the Doctor must do for the rest of his life?
choices: Cut wood for the palace fires every day
Look after the King's cattle in the fields
Scrub the King's kitchen-floor
Cook for the soldiers
questions.evidence: This Doctor shall scrub my kitchen-floor for the rest of his life!

questions.q: What did it mean when Polynesia said nothing and blinked her eyes?
choices: She was tired and was falling asleep in the tree
Someone had made trouble, and she was thinking of a way to put things right
She was frightened and did not know what to do next to save the Doctor
She was sad because she missed her old home in Puddleby very much
questions.evidence: Whenever she said nothing and blinked her eyes

questions.q: Whose fault did Polynesia say it was that they got lost?
choices: Chee-Chee's, for going away to look for cocoanuts
The Doctor's, for not following the right path
Gub-Gub's, for running off the path after ginger-roots
Jip's, for chasing after a rabbit in the jungle
questions.evidence: He would keep running off the path hunting for ginger-roots.

questions.q: What was Prince Bumpo reading when he came into the garden?
choices: A letter from his mother, the Queen
A book of fairy-tales
A book of magic spells
A map of the Land of the Monkeys
questions.evidence: He carried a book of fairy-tales under his arm.

questions.q: Polynesia talks "in a small, high voice like a little girl." Why does she change her voice?
choices: To show Chee-Chee how well she could sing
So Bumpo would believe a fairy was speaking to him
Because she had caught a cold in the wet jungle
So the King's soldiers would not know where she was
questions.evidence: talking in a small, high voice like a little girl

questions.q: Who did Polynesia pretend to be when she spoke to Bumpo?
choices: The Queen of the Jungle, who lived in the tallest palm-tree
Tripsitinka, the Queen of the Fairies, hiding in a rose-bud
A good wizard who lived far away across the wide sea
Bumpo's old nurse, who used to tell him fairy stories
questions.evidence: 'tis I, Tripsitinka, the Queen of the Fairies

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: How the monkeys said goodbye to the Doctor at the river
How Chee-Chee looked everywhere for the Doctor in the jungle
How the Doctor was caught again and Polynesia began a plan to free him
How Prince Bumpo spent a long afternoon in the garden reading fairy-stories
questions.evidence: she was thinking out some way to put things right
